comment: SPEC 8.1's ladder as a table: `elapsed` is the held checkpoint's age under SPEC 15 -- the node's estimate of now, the largest lower bound it holds (each verified quorum time plus the monotonic time since it was learned), minus the checkpoint's quorum time; cases with `observed` give the (quorum time, learned-at) pairs and `now` that derive it -- `staleness` is the network's own from params, and `hard` is this node's local S_hard. The rule is `elapsed > staleness`, so the boundary is still fresh. A node with no corroborated instant has no clock and reports `unknown` rather than guessing. A case may carry its own `hard`, overriding the top-level one: zero means S_hard is NOT CONFIGURED, not a limit of zero, so such a node stays `degraded` however old the view gets rather than dropping every peer. The states are tested in SPEC 8.1's order and the first that holds is the answer: `hard_stale` comes BEFORE `fresh`, so a node whose own S_hard is tighter than the network's staleness goes hard-stale at its own limit -- see `hard-below-staleness`, which is the only case separating the two readings of the table
